\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ریزگرد} (rizgard)}{ریزگرد (rizgard)}]{\fa{ریزگرد} (rizgard) — fine dust (in the air), dust haze}

\label{lesson:FA-C478-rizgard}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for mild, then the Persian for to sunbathe.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ریزگرد}}
\textbf{\fa{ریزگرد}} (\emph{rizgard}) — \textquotedblleft{}fine dust (in the air), dust haze\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{به} \fa{خاطر} \fa{ریزگرد} \fa{مدرسه} \fa{ها} \fa{تعطیل} \fa{شدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Be khâter-e rizgard madrese-hâ ta'til shodand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Because of the dust haze the schools closed.
\end{quote}

Dust from the deserts is a serious problem in the west and south of the country.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rizgard} is a modern native compound of \emph{riz} 'fine, tiny' and \emph{gard} 'dust', which EtymDB lists.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rizgard}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rizgard}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{rizgard}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for mild, then the Persian for to sunbathe, then say \emph{rizgard} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گرد} \fa{و} \fa{خاک} (gard-o khâk)}{گرد و خاک (gard-o khâk)}]{\fa{گرد} \fa{و} \fa{خاک} (gard-o khâk) — dust}

\label{lesson:FA-C478-gard-o-khak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to sunbathe, then the Persian for fine dust.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گرد} \fa{و} \fa{خاک}}
\textbf{\fa{گرد} \fa{و} \fa{خاک}} (\emph{gard-o khâk}) — \textquotedblleft{}dust\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{باد} \fa{گرد} \fa{و} \fa{خاک} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{خانه} \fa{آورد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bâd gard-o khâk râ be khâne âvard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The wind blew dust into the house.
\end{quote}

\emph{gard} 'dust' + \emph{o} 'and' + \emph{khâk} 'earth'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gard-o khâk} is a native pair: \emph{gard} 'dust', which EtymDB lists, and \emph{khâk} 'earth', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{xāk} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to sunbathe, then the Persian for fine dust, then say \emph{gard-o khâk} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خشکسالی} (khoshksâli)}{خشکسالی (khoshksâli)}]{\fa{خشکسالی} (khoshksâli) — a drought}

\label{lesson:FA-C478-khoshksali}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for fine dust, then the Persian for dust.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خشکسالی}}
\textbf{\fa{خشکسالی}} (\emph{khoshksâli}) — \textquotedblleft{}a drought\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خشکسالی} \fa{به} \fa{کشاورزها} \fa{ضرر} \fa{زد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Khoshksâli be keshâvarz-hâ zarar zad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The drought hurt the farmers.
\end{quote}

\emph{khoshk} 'dry' + \emph{sâl} 'year' + \emph{-i}: a dry year.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khoshksâli} is a native compound of \emph{khoshk} 'dry', which EtymDB lists, \emph{sâl} 'year', from Middle Persian \emph{sāl} (EtymDB), and the ending \emph{-i}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for fine dust, then the Persian for dust, then say \emph{khoshksâli} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خشک} \fa{شدن} (khoshk shodan)}{خشک شدن (khoshk shodan)}]{\fa{خشک} \fa{شدن} (khoshk shodan) — to dry up; to dry}

\label{lesson:FA-C478-khoshk-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for dust, then the Persian for a drought.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خشک} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{خشک} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{khoshk shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to dry up; to dry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{تابستان} \fa{نهر} \fa{خشک} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar tâbestân nahr khoshk shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In summer the stream dried up.
\end{quote}

\emph{khoshk} 'dry' + \emph{shodan}. Of washing: \emph{lebâs-hâ khoshk shod}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khoshk shodan} is built from native \emph{khoshk} 'dry', which EtymDB lists, and the native verb \emph{shodan} 'to become'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مه} \fa{آلود} (mehâlud)}{مه آلود (mehâlud)}]{\fa{مه} \fa{آلود} (mehâlud) — foggy, misty}

\label{lesson:FA-C478-mehalud}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a drought, then the Persian for to dry up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مه} \fa{آلود}}
\textbf{\fa{مه} \fa{آلود}} (\emph{mehâlud}) — \textquotedblleft{}foggy, misty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{صبح} \fa{جاده} \fa{مه} \fa{آلود} \fa{بود} \fa{و} \fa{آهسته} \fa{رانندگی} \fa{کردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sobh jâdde mehâlud bud va âheste rânandegi kardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the morning the road was foggy and we drove slowly.
\end{quote}

\emph{meh} 'fog' + \emph{âlud} 'covered with', from \emph{âludan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mehâlud} is a native compound of inherited words: \emph{meh} 'fog', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{mēgh}, and \emph{âlud} 'covered, smeared', the past stem of \emph{âludan} 'to soil, to smear', as in \emph{âlude} 'polluted'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
